text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Lim Wee Kiak –  24 To ask the Minister for Health (a) whether public hospitals are allowed to reject patients referred by polyclinics because their residential addresses fall outside the healthcare cluster and, if so, what percentage of referrals are rejected for this reason; and (b) how will the Ministry assist such patients, including hospital staff, who may be denied access to their workplace's outpatient benefits due to their residential addresses.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how does the Ministry plan to improve the triage process for patients referred to public hospitals by polyclinics, ensuring transparent justifications for rejecting referrals; and (b) what plans does the Ministry have to ensure effective communication in cases of rejected referrals, while establishing appropriate channels for follow-up and resolution.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The polyclinics will discuss alternative arrangements with the patient, including making a referral to another institution where applicable.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Patients may also contact the polyclinic, hospital or the cluster's main appointment centre to seek clarification and assistance for their referrals.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I declare that I am a medical doctor at a public hospital.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I raise this in my capacity as Member of Parliament (MP), as I have Clementi residents who are concerned about the matter in this Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State if he can reassure the House that based on the Minister for Health's commitment last year during the March 2022 Committee of Supply debate on the Healthier SG concept.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Minister at the time said individuals will have a choice – you can choose whether to enrol or not in Healthier SG, you can choose whom to enrol with, even doctors who are far away from your home, there is a variety of reasons why some Singaporeans decide to do that, such as because the clinic may be nearer to your workplace, near your parents' place.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, my first supplementary question is, can the Ministry of Health (MOH) confirm that this choice will still be available to persons seeking to enrol in Healthier SG because someone may seek care with a family doctor nearer to their workplace or with their caregivers?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: At the time, I had raised Clementi residents' concerns whether it will become harder to seek specialist care in a hospital outside their own geographical cluster because sometimes, residents may seek to see a specialist at a hospital not next to their home, but where they are going to be cared for by a family member during their illness.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Can the Senior Minister of State assure us that this freedom of choice will still be available to patients seeking referral for specialist care from polyclinics?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Lastly, if there are situations arising that need appeal, can the Senior Minister of State assure us there will be options available for patients to raise the matter to MOH for further study?
